name: Cybernetics, the shared foundation
overview: Steering through feedback: how systems regulate themselves, and how observers are part of what they observe.
road: Norbert Wiener → W. Ross Ashby (requisite variety) → Heinz von Foerster (second-order cybernetics) → Maturana and Varela → Gordon Pask (conversation theory) → Paul Pangaro
mix: Gregory Bateson and Margaret Mead at the Macy Conferences, Stafford Beer
policy: Requisite variety as a design test: services must match the variety of people's lives. Beer's Project Cybersyn is the classic, contested case of cybernetic government.

name: The formal science of complex systems
overview: Mathematical and computational study of emergence, networks, adaptation, and self-organization across physics, biology, and society.
road: Ilya Prigogine (dissipative structures) → Santa Fe Institute → network science (Barabási, Strogatz, Watts) → NECSI (Yaneer Bar-Yam)
mix: Hermann Haken (†2024, synergetics), Stuart Kauffman
policy: Agent-based models and network analysis of service systems, epidemics, and markets to test policy before rollout.

name: Relational, transcontextual, and post-humanist knowing
overview: Knowing through relationships rather than parts. Attends to how contexts shape each other and questions the human-centered, modern frame itself.
road: Gregory Bateson (Steps to an Ecology of Mind) → Nora Bateson (Warm Data, Combining) → Bayo Akomolafe (These Wilds Beyond Our Fences) → Vanessa Machado de Oliveira (Hospicing Modernity)
mix: Tyson Yunkaporta (Sand Talk), Donna Haraway (Staying with the Trouble), Karen Barad (agential realism), Isabelle Stengers. Joanna Macy (†2025) bridged systems theory, Buddhism, and deep ecology.
policy: Shows how policy categories fragment lived lives. Warm Data Labs with public teams, and the practice of hospicing institutions that no longer serve.

name: Nora Bateson and Warm Data
overview: Writer, filmmaker, and President of the International Bateson Institute. She carries her father Gregory's ecology of mind into living practice through Warm Data: information about the interrelationships that bind a complex system, found only by moving across contexts.
road: Gregory Bateson → An Ecology of Mind (film, 2010) → Small Arcs of Larger Circles (2016) → Warm Data Labs and host trainings → Combining (2023). Key ideas: transcontextual inquiry, symmathesy (mutual learning within living systems), aphanipoiesis (unseen coalescence toward vitality).
mix: Bayo Akomolafe, Tyson Yunkaporta, Otto Scharmer (as a structured counterpoint), the hosting practices
policy: Warm Data Labs hosted with public staff and residents change how people inside the system perceive and relate to an issue. Whatever policy or design follows comes from that shifted ground in its own time, not from findings harvested and handed over.

name: Indigenous and land-based knowledge
overview: Knowledge held in relationship with land, kin, and story, where reciprocity and pattern are themselves ways of knowing.
road: Vine Deloria Jr. → Gregory Cajete (Native Science) → Robin Wall Kimmerer (Braiding Sweetgrass, the Honorable Harvest) → Tyson Yunkaporta (Sand Talk)
mix: Leroy Little Bear, Winona LaDuke, Elinor Ostrom on the commons
policy: Indigenous-led stewardship and co-management of land and water, reciprocity as a design principle, and consultation that shares power instead of extracting input.

links.t: Center for Native Peoples and the Environment

name: Presencing, Theory U, and Social Presencing Theater
overview: Change that starts by suspending habitual seeing, sensing the whole, and letting new possibilities take form through the group.
road: Kurt Lewin (action research) → Argyris and Schön → Peter Senge → Otto Scharmer (Theory U, shaped in part by his interviews with Francisco Varela) → Arawana Hayashi (Social Presencing Theater, sensing a system through embodied movement)
mix: David Bohm (On Dialogue), Katrin Kaufer, Adam Kahane (transformative scenario planning)
policy: Co-sensing with residents and frontline staff before anything is designed. u.lab runs are widely used by public teams. Social Presencing Theater is hosted as embodied sensing, not as a technique for gathering input.

name: The metacrisis and meaning
overview: Treats interlocking ecological, social, and epistemic crises as one pattern rooted in how modern culture perceives and makes meaning.
road: Bateson and Edgar Morin (†2026) → Iain McGilchrist (The Matter with Things) → Jonathan Rowson (Perspectiva) → Zak Stein and John Vervaeke
mix: Vanessa Machado de Oliveira, Nora Bateson
policy: Long-horizon governance, and the sensemaking and meaning-making capacity democracies need to handle intertwined crises.

name: Living systems and regeneration
overview: Life as self-producing and interdependent, applied to ecological resilience and regenerative design of cultures and economies.
road: Maturana and Varela (autopoiesis) → Fritjof Capra → Daniel Christian Wahl (Designing Regenerative Cultures), alongside C.S. Holling → Carl Folke (resilience)
mix: Donella Meadows, Joanna Macy
policy: Resilience planning, climate adaptation, and bioregional thinking that treats places as living systems.

name: Sensemaking and acting in uncertainty
overview: Practical frameworks for telling ordered problems from complex ones and acting through small, safe-to-fail probes.
road: W. Ross Ashby → Karl Weick (†2026) → Alicia Juarrero → Dave Snowden (Cynefin) → Glenda Eoyang (Human Systems Dynamics)
mix: Stacey and Shaw's complex responsive processes
policy: Cynefin in policy and national risk work, safe-to-fail probes instead of big pilots, and distributed citizen narratives as live evidence.

name: Governance and self-organizing structures
overview: Designing decision structures that use feedback, consent, and distributed authority instead of command and control.
road: Ashby → Stafford Beer (Viable System Model) → Kees Boeke and Gerard Endenburg (†2025, sociocracy) → Elinor Ostrom (polycentric governance)
mix: Frederic Laloux, the Buurtzorg case, Indy Johar (Dark Matter Labs)
policy: Ostrom's design principles for co-governance of shared resources, polycentric arrangements across agencies, and consent-based structures inside teams.

name: Emergence in movements and social change
overview: How small, relational, adaptive actions scale into systemic change without central control.
road: Grace Lee Boggs and Octavia Butler → adrienne maree brown (Emergent Strategy) → Margaret Wheatley and the Berkana Two Loops model
mix: Nora Bateson on change that happens between contexts
policy: Governments hosting rather than directing: funding networks, backing community-led pilots, and using the Two Loops model to steward transitions.

name: Hosting and participatory practice
overview: Methods for convening groups so that collective intelligence and new patterns can emerge from the room.
road: Harrison Owen (Open Space) → Juanita Brown and David Isaacs (World Café) → Art of Hosting (Toke Møller, Chris Corrigan) → Liberating Structures (Lipmanowicz and McCandless) → Warm Data Labs
mix: David Bohm (On Dialogue), sociocracy, Social Presencing Theater
policy: Participatory processes, citizens' assemblies, and deliberative forums, with Art of Hosting methods long used in public institutions.

name: Bohm Dialogue
overview: Groups suspending assumptions and attending to collective thought as it moves, with no agenda or decision to reach.
road: David Bohm (On Dialogue) → William Isaacs (Dialogue and the Art of Thinking Together) → Peter Senge's learning organization work
mix: Otto Scharmer, Nora Bateson, the hosting practices
policy: Dialogue held for its own sake in cross-agency and community settings, with no decision on the table. Over time it loosens the assumptions that would otherwise harden into policy.

reading.title: The art of dialogue (MIT, on William Isaacs's Dialogue Project)

name: T-groups and sensitivity training
overview: Small unstructured groups learning from their own here-and-now interaction. The root of much of organization development.
road: Kurt Lewin → NTL Institute at Bethel, Maine (1947) → Chris Argyris and Edgar Schein (†2023) → Stanford's Interpersonal Dynamics course
mix: Group Relations, action research
policy: Leadership development that builds capacity to notice group dynamics, power, and feedback inside public teams.

name: Group Relations
overview: Temporary learning institutions where members study authority, role, and unconscious group dynamics as they happen.
road: Wilfred Bion (Experiences in Groups) → A.K. Rice and the Tavistock Institute's Leicester Conference (since 1957) → the A.K. Rice Institute in the US
mix: T-groups, systems psychodynamics
policy: Understanding authority and role in bureaucracies, and why systems unconsciously resist the change they commission.

name: Appreciative Inquiry
overview: Change that starts from what already gives life to a system rather than from its problems.
road: David Cooperrider and Suresh Srivastva (Case Western, 1980s) → the 4-D cycle → Appreciative Inquiry Summits for whole-system change
mix: Positive deviance, World Café
policy: Whole-system summits with residents, staff, and partners that design from existing strengths.

name: Work That Reconnects
overview: A group practice that moves through gratitude, honoring pain for the world, seeing with new eyes, and going forth.
road: Joanna Macy (†2025) → Molly Young Brown and facilitators worldwide → the Work That Reconnects Network
mix: Deep ecology, the relational pathway
policy: Sustaining public servants and communities working on climate and loss, where despair blocks action.

name: Somatic and embodied practice
overview: Change that lives in the body: how bodies hold history, shape what we can perceive under stress, and settle enough to act together. Treats embodiment as a condition for working in complexity, not a wellness add-on.
road: Wilhelm Reich and body-oriented psychology → Richard Strozzi-Heckler (somatic leadership) → Staci K. Haines (generative somatics, The Politics of Trauma) → Resmaa Menakem (My Grandmother's Hands, cultural somatics)
mix: Arawana Hayashi (Social Presencing Theater), Joanna Macy, the crisis and transition cluster
policy: Trauma-informed services and workplaces, frontline staff regulation in high-stress roles, and noticing how bodies in a room shape what a public meeting can actually hear.

links.t: Staci K. Haines: What is social justice somatics?

name: Power analysis
overview: Making power visible: who decides, whose issues never reach the table, and which beliefs make an arrangement feel natural. The missing question in much systems work.
road: Steven Lukes (Power: A Radical View, three faces of power) → John Gaventa (Power Cube: spaces, places, and forms of power) → Lisa VeneKlasen and Valerie Miller (A New Weave of Power, JASS)
mix: Paulo Freire, Michel Foucault, Sasha Costanza-Chock, Group Relations
policy: Mapping who actually shapes a policy, which consultations are closed, invited, or claimed spaces, and where invisible power (norms, beliefs) keeps residents out.

name: Narrative change
overview: Shifting the deep stories a society uses to make sense of an issue, so different policies become thinkable. Works over years through many voices, not one campaign.
road: George Lakoff (framing) → FrameWorks Institute (strategic frame analysis) → Narrative Initiative (Toward New Gravity) → Marshall Ganz (public narrative: story of self, us, and now)
mix: adrienne maree brown, Bayo Akomolafe, Hilary Cottam
policy: Reframing public problems so structural causes become visible, and giving public servants and residents a way to tell a shared story of why change is needed now.

links.t: FrameWorks Institute: Five questions about framing

name: Conflict transformation
overview: Treating conflict as information about a system and a doorway into changed relationships, rather than a problem to settle quickly. Holds justice and relationship together.
road: John Paul Lederach (The Moral Imagination) → Arnold and Amy Mindell (Deep Democracy, Worldwork) → Howard Zehr (restorative justice) → Marshall Rosenberg (Nonviolent Communication)
mix: Group Relations, T-groups, the somatic pathway, adrienne maree brown
policy: Restorative approaches in justice, schools, and housing; community mediation; and hosting charged public meetings so minority voices are not steamrolled by consensus.

name: Crisis, disaster, and high reliability
overview: What people and organizations do when normal order breaks. Disasters tend to produce mutual aid, not panic, and the best-run high-risk organizations stay alert to small failures instead of trusting their plans.
road: Enrico Quarantelli (disaster sociology) → Karl Weick and Kathleen Sutcliffe (Managing the Unexpected, high reliability organizing) → Rebecca Solnit (A Paradise Built in Hell) → Daniel Aldrich (social capital in recovery) → Dean Spade (mutual aid)
mix: Cynefin's chaotic domain, the somatic pathway, Ostrom on self-organized commons
policy: Emergency management that works with spontaneous volunteers rather than against them, investing in neighborhood ties before disasters, and after-action learning without blame.

links.t: Weick and Sutcliffe: high reliability principles

name: Ritual, liminality, and transition
overview: Why ritual matters when systems change. Transitions pass through a threshold where old roles dissolve before new ones form, and communities have long held people through that in-between.
road: Arnold van Gennep (rites of passage) → Victor Turner (liminality, communitas) → William Bridges (endings, neutral zone, new beginnings) → Francis Weller (grief as communal work)
mix: Work That Reconnects, Bayo Akomolafe, Vanessa Machado de Oliveira (hospicing), Indigenous and land-based knowledge
policy: Marking endings when programs close or teams merge, grief and memorial work after a crisis, and treating reorganizations as transitions people move through, not org charts.

links.t: William Bridges Associates: What is transition?
Francis Weller: The Geography of Sorrow (The Sun)

name: Public policy and government innovation
overview: Moving public management from targets and linear delivery toward learning, relationships, experimentation, and adaptive stewardship.
road: Rittel and Webber (wicked problems) → Donella Meadows (leverage points) → Geoff Mulgan (collective intelligence, public imagination) → Toby Lowe (Human Learning Systems) → Hilary Cottam (Radical Help, the relational state)
mix: Mariana Mazzucato (mission-oriented policy), Christian Bason (design for policy), Indy Johar (Dark Matter Labs), Bill Sharpe (Three Horizons), UNDP's portfolio approach to systems change
policy: This is the home field for the policy lens. Read it alongside the Strategy, money, and accountability cluster, where budgets, contracts, and metrics decide whether any of this survives contact with a real institution.

links.t: UCL Institute for Innovation and Public Purpose
OECD Observatory of Public Sector Innovation

name: Systemic design and futures
overview: Design practice scaled up to whole systems, paired with ways of using the future to act differently in the present.
road: Horst Rittel → Birger Sevaldson (gigamapping) → Hugh Dubberly and Paul Pangaro → Riel Miller (futures literacy) → Bill Sharpe (Three Horizons)
mix: Dan Hill (Dark Matter and Trojan Horses), Christian Bason, Dunne and Raby (critical design), Stuart Candy (experiential futures)
policy: Government policy labs, anticipatory governance, futures literacy for civil servants, and portfolio approaches instead of single-bet programs.

name: Complexity economics and new economic models
overview: The economy as an evolving, adaptive system of people and institutions rather than an equilibrium machine.
road: Herbert Simon (bounded rationality) → W. Brian Arthur (increasing returns) → Eric Beinhocker (The Origin of Wealth) → Kate Raworth (Doughnut Economics)
mix: J. Doyne Farmer (Making Sense of Chaos), Elinor Ostrom, Mariana Mazzucato
policy: City Doughnut portraits (Amsterdam adopted the model in 2020), mission-oriented innovation, and regulation that expects adaptation.

name: Strategy under uncertainty
overview: Strategy that assumes the future cannot be predicted: rehearse several futures, map how value chains evolve, and build options that benefit from surprise.
road: Pierre Wack (Shell scenarios) → Adam Kahane (transformative scenario planning) → Simon Wardley (Wardley Mapping) → Nassim Nicholas Taleb (antifragility)
mix: Three Horizons, Cynefin, futures literacy
policy: Scenario work before long-lived infrastructure or budget commitments, and mapping which public capabilities are commodity versus genuinely new before procuring them.

links.t: Pierre Wack: Scenarios, Uncharted Waters Ahead (HBR)
Adam Kahane: Transformative Scenario Planning (SSIR excerpt)

name: Funding and budgeting for adaptation
overview: Money that can follow learning. Replaces fixed annual budgets and single big bets with rolling allocation, portfolios of experiments, and funders who trust grantees.
road: Jeremy Hope and Robin Fraser (Beyond Budgeting) → Bjarte Bogsnes (Equinor) → UNDP portfolio approach → Trust-Based Philanthropy Project
mix: Human Learning Systems, developmental evaluation, Mariana Mazzucato
policy: Multi-year flexible funding, portfolio budgets for missions, and grant terms that let providers change course when they learn something.

links.t: Bogsnes: Beyond Budgeting at Equinor (Drucker Forum)
UNDP: portfolio approach to system transformation

name: Measurement and accountability
overview: Why targets distort what they measure, and what accountability can look like when outcomes are emergent. Moves from proving results to learning in public.
road: Donald Campbell and Charles Goodhart (the laws named after them) → Mark Moore (public value, the strategic triangle) → Jerry Muller (The Tyranny of Metrics) → Toby Lowe (accountability for learning)
mix: Deming, developmental evaluation, Human Learning Systems
policy: Replacing target regimes with learning reviews, reporting what changed and why, and holding services accountable for the health of relationships and systems, not activity counts.

links.t: Jerry Muller: The Tyranny of Metrics (Chronicle)
Moore's strategic triangle (Atlas of Public Management)

name: Government plumbing
overview: The rules, contracts, and routines where reluctant bureaucracies actually push back. Procurement, delivery, regulation, and frontline discretion decide whether complexity methods survive.
road: Michael Lipsky (Street-Level Bureaucracy) → Charles Sabel and Jonathan Zeitlin (experimentalist governance) → relational commissioning (Plymouth Alliance) → Jennifer Pahlka (Recoding America)
mix: Nesta on anticipatory regulation and sandboxes, Hilary Cottam, service design
policy: Alliance contracts instead of payment by results, policy written with delivery teams at the table, regulatory sandboxes, and trusting frontline discretion instead of scripting it away.

name: Teams and learning cultures
overview: The team-level conditions that let people surface bad news, learn fast, and organize around flow instead of hierarchy.
road: Amy Edmondson (psychological safety, teaming) → Jeff Gothelf and Josh Seiden (Sense and Respond) → Matthew Skelton and Manuel Pais (Team Topologies)
mix: Deming, sociocracy, T-groups
policy: Blameless reviews in public agencies, product teams that own a service end to end, and outcomes over outputs in digital delivery.

links.t: Amy Edmondson: Building a psychologically safe workplace (TEDx)

name: Corporate innovation and renewal
overview: How established organizations explore new value while running the current business, and when they need to break apart into smaller self-managing units.
road: Clayton Christensen (disruptive innovation) → Charles O'Reilly and Michael Tushman (ambidextrous organization) → Henry Chesbrough (open innovation) → Haier (RenDanHeYi microenterprises)
mix: Buurtzorg, Beyond Budgeting, Wardley Mapping
policy: Public agencies face the same exploit and explore tension: protected space for new services without starving the ones residents rely on today.

name: Collaboration across boundaries
overview: How many organizations work on one shared problem without one of them owning it. The field has moved from shared measurement toward equity and community power.
road: John Kania and Mark Kramer (collective impact, 2011) → Mark Cabaj and Liz Weaver (Collective Impact 3.0) → Collective Impact Forum's equity turn
mix: Ostrom, network weaving, Two Loops, Human Learning Systems
policy: Cross-agency place-based partnerships, shared learning agendas instead of shared KPIs, and residents holding real seats in governance.

name: Design thinking
overview: Framing problems through empathy, prototyping, and iteration. Strong for bounded problems, weaker where no single solution exists.
road: Herbert Simon (The Sciences of the Artificial) → Horst Rittel → Nigel Cross (Designerly Ways of Knowing) → Donald Schön (reflection-in-action) → IDEO and the Stanford d.school
mix: Natasha Iskander's critique of design thinking
policy: Human-centered problem framing in agency innovation teams. Most useful when paired with complexity methods for problems without one right answer.

name: Service design
overview: Services as journeys across touchpoints, with frontstage experience and backstage systems designed together.
road: Lynn Shostack (service blueprinting) → Birgit Mager (Köln) → Marc Stickdorn (This Is Service Design Doing) → Lou Downe (Good Services)
mix: UK Government Digital Service, US Digital Service, 18F (closed 2025)
policy: End-to-end benefit and permit journeys, service standards, and blueprints that expose the policy and system constraints behind a bad experience.

name: Participatory design and design justice
overview: Designing with people rather than for them, with power named and shared in the process.
road: Scandinavian participatory design (Pelle Ehn, Kristen Nygaard) → Elizabeth Sanders (co-design) → Ezio Manzini (Design, When Everybody Designs) → Sasha Costanza-Chock (Design Justice) → Arturo Escobar (Designs for the Pluriverse)
mix: The relational and Indigenous pathways
policy: Co-designing programs with the residents they serve, with explicit attention to who holds decision power.

name: Transition design
overview: Design for long-horizon societal transitions, grounded in living systems theory. The design path most explicitly built on complexity.
road: Terry Irwin, Gideon Kossoff, and Cameron Tonkinwise (Carnegie Mellon)
mix: Three Horizons, Capra, Meadows
policy: Long-horizon transitions in energy, food, and care that span agencies and election cycles.

name: Strategic design and policy labs
overview: Using design to reshape institutions and the rules, budgets, and culture underneath them.
road: Helsinki Design Lab (Sitra, Bryan Boyer, Dan Hill) and MindLab (Christian Bason) → Policy Lab UK and La 27e Région → Dark Matter Labs
mix: Geoff Mulgan, Nesta
policy: In-house policy labs and stewardship models that change procurement, budgeting, and governance, not just services.

name: Improvement and adaptive management
overview: Learning cycles built into daily operations, treating the organization as a system to be continually improved.
road: W. Edwards Deming (System of Profound Knowledge) → Toyota and Lean → Don Berwick and IHI (PDSA cycles) → Agile
mix: Plexus Institute's healthcare work, Brenda Zimmerman
policy: PDSA cycles in public health and service delivery, and continuous improvement units inside agencies.

name: Developmental evaluation
overview: Evaluation built for innovation in complex settings, feeding real-time learning instead of judging afterward.
road: Michael Quinn Patton → Mark Cabaj and the Tamarack Institute
mix: Human Learning Systems, Cynefin
policy: Funding and accountability for adaptive programs, where evaluators help programs learn while they run.

name: Action research
overview: Inquiry and change as one act, led with and by the people affected.
road: Kurt Lewin → Paulo Freire and Orlando Fals-Borda (participatory action research) → Peter Reason and Hilary Bradbury
mix: Chris Argyris (action science), the hosting pathway
policy: Community-led inquiry into local problems, with residents as co-researchers and co-owners of findings.

links.t: Action Research Network of the Americas

name: Positive deviance
overview: Finding the uncommon practices that already work inside a community and helping them spread.
road: Jerry and Monique Sternin
mix: Plexus Institute, which championed it in healthcare
policy: Scaling what already works in the field, from frontline caseworkers to communities, before importing outside solutions.

name: Experiential learning and reflective practice
overview: Learning as a cycle of doing, noticing, making sense, and trying again. The base layer for learning complexity, because complexity is mostly learned by acting and reflecting.
road: John Dewey → Kurt Lewin → David Kolb (the experiential learning cycle) → Donald Schön (reflection-in-action)
mix: Action research, T-groups, improvement cycles
policy: Learning built into delivery: reflective supervision for frontline staff, learning reviews after each cycle, and training that happens on real cases.

links.t: David A. Kolb on experiential learning (infed)
Kurt Lewin: groups, experiential learning, and action research (infed)

name: Transformative learning
overview: Learning that changes the frame, not just the content. Often starts with a disorienting dilemma and moves through critical reflection toward a new perspective. Threshold concepts name the ideas that are troublesome before they become obvious.
road: Jack Mezirow (perspective transformation) → Edward Taylor and Patricia Cranton → Jan Meyer and Ray Land (threshold concepts and troublesome knowledge)
mix: Freire, Robert Kegan, Nora Bateson on education
policy: Designing public-sector learning so staff can revisit core assumptions, not just learn new procedures, especially when a service model is changing.

links.t: Taylor: The Theory and Practice of Transformative Learning (ERIC)
The Value of Troublesome Knowledge (Composition Forum)

name: Critical and popular education
overview: Education as practice of freedom: learners read their own world, name the forces shaping it, and act together. Popular education schools trained the movements that changed laws.
road: Paulo Freire (Pedagogy of the Oppressed, conscientization) → Myles Horton and the Highlander Folk School → bell hooks (Teaching to Transgress, engaged pedagogy)
mix: Orlando Fals-Borda, Grace Lee Boggs, power analysis
policy: Community education that builds residents' own analysis before consultation, and civic learning that treats people as co-authors of policy.

links.t: Paulo Freire: dialogue, praxis and education (infed)
How Myles Horton built a social movement institution (Convergence)

name: Communities of practice and action learning
overview: Learning held by groups of practitioners over time. Communities of practice share a domain; action learning sets meet to work on real problems through questions rather than advice.
road: Reg Revans (action learning, learning equals programmed knowledge plus questioning) → Jean Lave and Etienne Wenger (communities of practice) → Etienne and Beverly Wenger-Trayner (social learning, systems convening)
mix: Art of Hosting, Human Learning Systems, developmental evaluation
policy: Cross-agency practitioner communities, peer learning networks between cities, and action learning sets for managers facing problems with no known answer.

links.t: Wenger-Trayner: Introduction to communities of practice
Revans Action Learning archive (University of Salford)

name: Adult development and immunity to change
overview: How adults grow in their capacity to hold complexity, and why people stay stuck even when they want to change. Stages describe how someone makes meaning, not how much they are worth.
road: Jean Piaget → Robert Kegan (In Over Our Heads) → Kegan and Lisa Lahey (immunity to change) → Jennifer Garvey Berger (Simple Habits for Complex Times)
mix: Transformative learning, Group Relations, Theory U
policy: Leadership programs that work with competing commitments behind stalled reforms, without turning developmental stages into a ranking of staff.

links.t: Kegan and Lahey: The Real Reason People Won't Change (HBR)
Simple Habits for Complex Times (Cultivating Leadership)

name: Complexity and education
overview: Treating classrooms, schools, and learning programs as complex systems in their own right, and asking what it takes to educate people for a world that cannot be predicted.
road: Edgar Morin (Seven Complex Lessons in Education for the Future) → Brent Davis and Dennis Sumara (Complexity and Education) → Nora Bateson on education → Inner Development Goals (a widely used capacity framework)
mix: The Systems Change Learning Guide's learning areas, communities of practice, threshold concepts
policy: Public education and workforce programs that teach uncertainty, relationship, and systems literacy alongside content, and that evaluate learning developmentally.

links.t: Morin: Seven complex lessons in education for the future (UNESCO)
Nora Bateson: Preparing for a confusing future
